--- title: "Foundations 02 — Data Types and Data Structures" subtitle: "STAT/DATA 1810 · Week 2 Monday · SOLUTION" author: "Instructor key" format: html: toc: true execute: warning: false message: false --- ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) ``` ::: # 0 · The one distinction, and your own chunks (8 min) Write the sentence on the board and leave it there all class: **type = one value's nature; structure = the container.** **Teaching note — inserting chunks.** Demonstrate the shortcut (Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + I) *once*, slowly, on the projector: cursor on a blank line, press it, the fence appears, type `1 + 1`, run. Then YT0 — walk the room for 2 minutes and make sure every screen shows output under a student-made chunk before moving on. This is the one thing today that can't be caught up on later; every later YT depends on it. Students who type the fence by hand are fine — the skill is "I can make a chunk," not the shortcut. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # YT0 1 + 1 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 2 ``` ::: ::: # 1 · Data types (22 min) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM1 — expected: "numeric", "integer", "character", "logical" class(4.75) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "numeric" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} class(4L) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "integer" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} class("latte") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "character" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} class(TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "logical" ``` ::: ::: **Q1 note:** most students predict `"numeric"` for `4L` — good; the surprise is the point. The `L` suffix is worth 30 seconds, no more. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM2 — "double" vs "integer" typeof(4.75) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "double" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} typeof(4L) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "integer" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM3 — factor with 3 levels class(iris$Species) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "factor" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} levels(iris$Species) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "setosa" "versicolor" "virginica" ``` ::: ::: **Q2:** 3 levels — setosa, versicolor, virginica. **Teaching note:** the menu metaphor ("a factor is text with a fixed menu") pays rent in week 6 when forcats arrives. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM4 today <- Sys.Date() class(today) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Date" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} right_now <- Sys.time() class(right_now) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt" ``` ::: ::: Expected classes: `"Date"` and `"POSIXct" "POSIXt"` — say "date-time" and move on; lubridate handles the ugliness in week 4. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM5 sum(is.na(airquality$Ozone)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 37 ``` ::: ::: **Q3: 37 missing.** Real 1973 NYC air data — the missing values are genuinely missing, not planted. First appearance of the `is.na()` + `sum()` idiom; students will use it in every cycle. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM6 — any correct fills, e.g. is.numeric(4.75) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} is.character("latte") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} is.logical(TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} is.factor(iris$Species) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # YT1 — expected: "character", "logical", "numeric", "Date" class("TRUE") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "character" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} class(3 > 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "logical" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} class(mtcars$cyl) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "numeric" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} class(Sys.Date() + 7) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Date" ``` ::: ::: **YT1 teaching note:** the surprise is almost always `"TRUE"` — quotes make it text. Second surprise: `3 > 2` *produces* a logical; comparisons are how logicals get made in practice (filter() in two weeks). `mtcars$cyl` being numeric though it only takes 4/6/8 is a preview of activity item E. # 2 · Data structures (30 min) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM7 drinks <- c("latte", "drip", "mocha") drinks ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "latte" "drip" "mocha" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} length(drinks) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} class(drinks) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "character" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # YT2 prices <- c(4.75, 2.75, 5.25) sizes <- c("small", "medium", "large") iced <- c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE) prices; sizes; iced ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 4.75 2.75 5.25 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "small" "medium" "large" ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE FALSE TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} class(prices); class(sizes); class(iced) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "numeric" ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "character" ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "logical" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} c(1, "two", 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "1" "two" "3" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} class(c(1, "two", 3)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "character" ``` ::: ::: **Q4: character.** A vector holds *one* type, so R converts everything to the type that can hold all of it — text. This is **coercion**, arriving by accident rather than lecture. Say the word once; students meet it again when a numeric column imports as `` because of one stray "N/A". ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM8 menu_df <- data.frame(drink = drinks, price = c(4.75, 2.75, 5.25)) menu_tbl <- tibble(drink = drinks, price = c(4.75, 2.75, 5.25)) menu_df ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} menu_tbl ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: **Q5 model answers (any one):** the tibble announces its dimensions (`# A tibble: 3 × 2`); the tibble shows column types (``, ``); the data frame shows row numbers without types. **Framing:** a tibble IS a data frame with better manners — we'll say "data frame" for both. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # YT3 menu <- tibble(drink = drinks, price = prices, size = sizes, iced = iced) menu ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} nrow(menu); ncol(menu); class(menu) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 4 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "tbl_df" "tbl" "data.frame" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # YT3 — the deliberate break tibble(drink = drinks, price = c(4.75, 2.75)) #> Error: Tibble columns must have compatible sizes. #> • Size 3: Existing data. #> • Size 2: Column `price`. ``` ::: **YT3 teaching note:** the error is a *good* error — it names the sizes and the column. Have someone read it aloud. "Every column the same length" is now something they've felt, not heard. (`class(menu)` returns three things — `tbl_df`, `tbl`, `data.frame` — say "it's a data frame, with extra labels" and move on.) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM9 — tribble, briefly tribble( ~drink, ~price, "chai", 4.50, "espresso", 3.00 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM10 — list my_list <- list(name = "week 2", nums = c(1, 2, 3), data = menu_tbl) my_list ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` $name [1] "week 2" $nums [1] 1 2 3 $data # A tibble: 3 × 2 drink price 1 latte 4.75 2 drip 2.75 3 mocha 5.25 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} length(my_list) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ::: **Junk-drawer framing:** a list holds anything, including a whole tibble. `length()` is 3 — three drawers, whatever's inside them. Plant the flag: *"when we pull data from an API in week 8, it arrives as a list."* ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # YT4 — e.g. me <- list(first = "Eman", n_classes = 4, menu = menu) me ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` $first [1] "Eman" $n_classes [1] 4 $menu # A tibble: 3 × 4 drink price size iced 1 latte 4.75 small TRUE 2 drip 2.75 medium FALSE 3 mocha 5.25 large TRUE ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM11 — matrix, briefly matrix(1:6, nrow = 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] [,2] [,3] [1,] 1 3 5 [2,] 2 4 6 ``` ::: ::: **Q6:** a data frame — a matrix forces every cell to one type, so names + numbers would coerce the numbers to text (same coercion as Q4, now at the structure level). # 3 · In-class activity (15 min) One chunk per item — check that students actually made six chunks; the habit of "one idea, one chunk" is what makes ETV documents readable. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # A — Structure class(iris) # "data.frame" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "data.frame" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # B — Type class(iris$Sepal.Length) # "numeric" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "numeric" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # C — Type question (is.na tests values) sum(is.na(airquality$Solar.R)) # 7 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 7 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # D — Structure built by the student, e.g. foods_tbl <- tibble( food = c("tacos", "pho", "pizza"), rating = c(10, 9, 8) ) foods_tbl ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # E — Type; stored as integer, arguably should be a factor (or a Date) class(airquality$Month) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "integer" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # F — Structure: a list holding a tibble and a vector food_places <- list( foods = foods_tbl, places = c("truck on Higuera", "home", "campus") ) food_places ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` $foods # A tibble: 3 × 2 food rating 1 tacos 10 2 pho 9 3 pizza 8 $places [1] "truck on Higuera" "home" "campus" ``` ::: ::: **Answers: A = S · B = T · C = T (7 missing) · D = S · E = T ("integer"; a factor would make sense since 5–9 are labels, not amounts) · F = S.** E is the discussion item: *the type R stores is not always the type the data means* — that's the whole reason `mutate()` + `factor()` exists. # 4 · Exit question (5 min) **Model answer:** "A data type is what one value is — `4.75` is numeric. A data structure is the container holding values — my `menu` tibble is a data frame whose `iced` column is logical." Any answer pairing one correct type example with one correct structure example passes; at least one example should be from a student-built object.
